<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">In the era of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), enhancing multimodal reasoning capabilities remains a critical challenge, particularly in handling ambiguous or complex visual inputs, where initial inferences often lead to hallucinations or logic errors. Existing VLMs often produce plausible yet ungrounded answers, and even when prompted to “reflect”, their corrections may remain detached from the image evidence. To address this, we propose the <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR</span> framework for <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">m</span>ultimodal <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">i</span>terative <span id="abstract1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">r</span>easoning via <span id="abstract1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">r</span>eflection <span id="abstract1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">o</span>n visual <span id="abstract1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">r</span>egions. By embedding visual reflection as a core mechanism, MIRROR is formulated as a closed-loop process comprising draft, critique, region-based verification, and revision, which are repeated until the output is visually grounded. To facilitate training of this model, we construct <span id="abstract1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ReflectV</span>, a visual reflective dataset for multi-turn supervision that explicitly contains reflection triggers, region-based verification actions, and answer revision grounded in visual evidence. Experiments on both general vision-language benchmarks and representative vision-language reasoning benchmarks show that MIRROR improves correctness and reduces visual hallucinations, demonstrating the value of training reflection as an evidence-seeking, region-aware verification process rather than a purely textual revision step.</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Keywords: </h6>Vision-Language Model, Visual Reflection, Iterative Reasoning, Thinking with Images
</div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="p1.1.1" class="ltx_text"><span id="p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Project Page:</span> <a href="https://mirror.github.io/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://mirror.github.io/</a></span></p>
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent years have witnessed the rapid evolution of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), which integrate powerful visual encoders with Large Language Models (LLMs) to achieve remarkable performance in general multimodal tasks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Peng et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Despite these advancements, enhancing multimodal reasoning capabilities remains a critical challenge, particularly when handling ambiguous or complex visual inputs. To address this, paradigms such as Chain-of-Thought <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and “Thinking with Images” <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Su et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> have been introduced to align logical generation with visual contexts. However, in complex scenarios, the reasoning process still leads to plausible yet ungrounded answers, a phenomenon widely known as hallucination <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guan et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Reflection serves as a critical mechanism in robust multimodal reasoning, refining initial inferences to ensure logical accuracy. Current approaches have attempted to model this process by incorporating the CoT mechanisms <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and self-correction strategies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025d</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wan et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. While these methods improve robustness to some extent, they fundamentally suffer from a “modality disconnect”: they largely rely on textual revision. Even when prompted to “reflect”, the model’s corrections often remain detached from the actual image evidence. Without an explicit mechanism to revisit visual details, models tend to hallucinate “corrections” based on linguistic priors rather than visual facts.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper, we argue that overcoming this limitation requires a paradigm shift: reflection for VLMs must be transformed from an open-loop text generation step into a closed-loop grounded verification process. This perspective draws inspiration from human cognitive behavior—specifically the instinct to “look again” when detecting ambiguity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Aligned with the philosophy of “Thinking with Images”, we argue that an ideal system should possess the capability of closed-loop verification. The model should not only detect logical errors but also actively re-examine the image to find evidence, thereby ensuring reasoning is visually grounded.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18746v1/teaser.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/289;" width="476" height="289" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Our visual reflective framework MIRROR improves visual question answering by iteratively verifying evidence in the image and revising the prediction. In each example, Round 1 produces an incorrect answer; the model then reflects with explicit visual grounding (e.g., yellow points/ purple ellipse) to re-check the relevant regions and corrects the response in Round 2, yielding a final accurate answer.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">To achieve this, we propose <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR</span>, a novel framework for <span id="S1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">m</span>ultimodal <span id="S1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">i</span>terative <span id="S1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">r</span>easoning via <span id="S1.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">r</span>eflection <span id="S1.p4.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">o</span>n visual <span id="S1.p4.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">r</span>egions, which regards visual reflection as a core mechanism, upgrading the inference process into a closed-loop verification cycle. Unlike traditional methods, MIRROR empowers the model to actively diagnose potential errors and utilize a tool-augmented visual prompt generator to check specific image regions, as shown in <a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. This process unfolds through a cycle of drafting, critiquing, region-based verification and revision, ensuring that every correction is anchored in concrete visual evidence. To instill this capability, we construct <span id="S1.p4.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ReflectV</span>, a visual reflective dataset of approximately 24k samples using a multi-agent pipeline. Ranging from general scene understanding to complex reasoning tasks, the dataset combines internal reflection with precise visual cues to teach the model <span id="S1.p4.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">how</span> to reflect visually.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We fine-tune Qwen2.5-VL on ReflectV
and evaluate its performance on both general vision-language and visual reasoning benchmarks. Experimental results show that MIRROR improves correctness and reduces hallucinations, demonstrating that reflection should be trained as an evidence-seeking process rather than a simple text revision step.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In summary, our main contributions are as follows:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose MIRROR, a visual reflective framework. It enables VLMs to perform closed-loop reasoning by iteratively triggering self-reflection and invoking a visual prompt generator to verify visual details, thereby reducing hallucinations in complex tasks.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We construct ReflectV, a high-quality dataset of approximately 24k samples. Through a novel multi-agent pipeline, we curate ReflectV that explicitly models the trajectory of error detection, visual verification, and answer correction.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We fine-tune Qwen2.5-VL on our dataset and obtain the <span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR</span> model. This model outperforms strong baselines across diverse vision-language benchmarks, demonstrating the efficacy of our closed-loop verification mechanism in reducing hallucinations and enhancing grounded reasoning.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Vision-Language Models</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent years have witnessed rapid progress of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), which connect a powerful visual encoder with a large language model (LLM) through lightweight adapters or cross-attention modules. Beyond generic image understanding, grounding and localization capabilities are increasingly integrated into VLMs to reduce hallucinations and support fine-grained visual reference. For example, LLaVA-NeXT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> leverages a dynamic high-resolution strategy to preserve subtle visual cues, while Kosmos-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Peng et al., 2023</a>)</cite> introduces a tokenization to represent grounded text spans linked to bounding boxes, allowing models to generate text grounded in image regions. Recent open-source VLMs such as Qwen2.5-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and InternVL3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> scale training data and refine alignment pipelines to improve instruction following, localization, OCR, and general visual-language competence. Regarding closed-source models, Gemini-3.0 Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Google, 2025</a>)</cite> and GPT-5.2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2025</a>)</cite> demonstrate strong general multimodal capabilities and inspire new reasoning patterns, motivating research on grounding and visual feedback. Building on the instruction-tuned VLM paradigm, our approach targets a more structured capability: enabling the model to execute a closed-loop reasoning process with iterative visual reflection.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Multimodal Reasoning in VLMs</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The paradigm of multimodal reasoning in VLMs has progressed significantly, evolving from standard instruction following to incorporating Chain-of-Thought (CoT) mechanisms <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2022</a>)</cite> that align logical generation with visual context, e.g., LLaVA-CoT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. To further enhance robustness and mitigate hallucinations, recent approaches have introduced self-correction strategies. For instance, Critique Fine-Tuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025d</a>)</cite> integrates explicit critique steps into the training objective, while methods like FIRE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024c</a>)</cite> employ “response-feedback-refinement” triplets to enable models to iteratively refine answers based on feedback signals. In parallel, research in visual grounding has employed visual prompts—such as bounding boxes and points—to enhance referential precision. Models like Shikra <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and SoM-GPT4V <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>)</cite> demonstrate that explicit visual markers can significantly aid in parsing fine-grained details. Beyond static visual grounding, recent work has begun to explore a broader <em id="S2.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">“Thinking with Images”</em> paradigm <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Su et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Su et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, where VLMs actively attend to visual evidence during reasoning to acquire finer-grained visual signals for verification. Nevertheless, prior works lack a <em id="S2.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">reflection-driven</em> control signal, while visual tool usage is rarely leveraged to rectify errors and enable targeted region verification.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>Reflection in Vision-language Models</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reflection aims to address core issues in VLMs, such as inadequate reasoning rigor, insufficient utilization of visual information, and difficulty in self-correcting errors. Relevant studies have explored solutions through optimizing reflection mechanisms, enhancing visual interaction, and integrating external knowledge. SRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wan et al., 2025</a>)</cite> introduces the <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle</annotation></semantics></math>reflection<math id="S2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> token and GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> to strengthen the model’s self-reflection capability. VL-Rethinker <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> adopts selective sample replay for effective data filtering and forced rethinking strategies, alleviating the diminishing reflection advantage. Look-Back <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> designs <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle</annotation></semantics></math>back<math id="S2.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> token to guide the model to revisit image information. Reflection-V <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jian et al., 2025</a>)</cite> leverages a cold-start supervised phase to extract visual details and then employs reinforcement learning with attention-aware rewards to incentivize the model’s focus on critical visual information. Additionally, some other studies attempt to improve reasoning performance through multi-agent collaboration (e.g., Mulberry <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>) or tool-chain expansion (e.g., Thyme <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18746v1/method.png" id="S2.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/211;" width="476" height="211" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S2.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">MIRROR performs closed-loop visual reflection. The VLM alternates between drafting an answer, reflecting, invoking a visual tool for region-level verification, and revising based on the rendered visual evidence.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">However, most existing approaches limit reflection to textual reflections or implicit representations, often failing to actively revisit visual evidence. In contrast, the proposed <span id="S2.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR</span> enables <span id="S2.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">explicit visual reflection</span>. By integrating visual tools, our framework transforms reflection from a static revision step into an active verification process, where the model explicitly queries and checks specific image regions to ensure every correction is visually grounded.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose <span id="S3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR</span> as shown in <a href="#S2.F2" title="In 2.3 Reflection in Vision-language Models ‣ 2 Related Work ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, a visual reflective framework that transforms one-pass VLM inference into a closed-loop verification process:
(i) draft an initial answer;
(ii) self-reflection to identify uncertainty or potential errors;
(iii) visual verification by invoking a visual prompt generator to mark task-relevant regions;
and (iv) refinement based on the updated visual evidence.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Formulation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We formulate the visual reflective reasoning task as a multi-turn generation process. Given an initial image <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and a user query <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, the objective of the VLM, denoted as <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, is to generate a structured reasoning trajectory <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{Y}=\{y_{1},y_{2},\dots,y_{K}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{Y}=\{y_{1},y_{2},\dots,y_{K}\}</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> interaction turns. Unlike standard CoT reasoning, which operates on static visual features, our framework incorporates dynamic visual interactions. At each step <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, the model generates an output tuple <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{k}=(a_{k},r_{k},v_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{k}=(a_{k},r_{k},v_{k})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is the textual response, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the reflection content, and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> signifies the visual tool tokens for visual reflection. The tool tokens <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> trigger a visual update function <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding an updated visual context <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{k}=\mathcal{G}(I_{0},v_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{k}=\mathcal{G}(I_{0},v_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> that highlights specific regions for the subsequent step. Consequently, for the <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(k+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(k+1)</annotation></semantics></math>-th turn, the model takes the updated visual context <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and the interaction history <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{&lt;k+1}=\{a_{j},r_{j},v_{j}\}_{j=1}^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{&lt;k+1}=\{a_{j},r_{j},v_{j}\}_{j=1}^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> as input to generate the next response tuple <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math>. This process can be formulated as:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{k+1}\sim\pi_{\theta}(y_{k+1}\mid I_{k},q,h_{&lt;k+1})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{k+1}\sim\pi_{\theta}(y_{k+1}\mid I_{k},q,h_{&lt;k+1})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{k+1}=(a_{k+1},r_{k+1},v_{k+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{k+1}=(a_{k+1},r_{k+1},v_{k+1})</annotation></semantics></math> represents the newly generated answer, reflection, and visual tool tokens. This loop repeats until the model’s reflection validates the answer.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Tool-Augmented Visual Prompt Generation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A key innovation of MIRROR is the integration of the visual prompt generator <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> for visual reflection. This module allows the model to actively “verify” its reflection by grounding textual hypotheses into crucial visual signals. The workflow proceeds as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Triggering the Tool:</span> When the model identifies some content in its reasoning chain for further verification, it initiates a request enclosed within a special token structure <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center">
<div id="S3.E2.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_markedasmath ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:258.8pt;height:98.8pt;vertical-align:-45.9pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(37.7pt,-14.4pt) scale(1.41179867409094,1.41179867409094) ;">
<p id="S3.E2.2.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.E2.m1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext='\begin{aligned} &amp;\texttt{&lt;tool\_call&gt;}\{\\
&amp;\quad\texttt{name}:\texttt{"Visual Prompt Generator"},\\
&amp;\quad\texttt{flag}:\texttt{true/false}\\
&amp;\quad\texttt{anchor}:\texttt{"keywords..."}\\
&amp;\quad\texttt{args}:\{\texttt{color}:\texttt{"red"},\texttt{shape}:\texttt{"point"}\}\\
&amp;\}\texttt{&lt;/tool\_call&gt;}\end{aligned}' display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="0pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;tool_call&gt;</mtext><mo stretchy="false">{</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">name</mtext><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">"Visual Prompt Generator"</mtext></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">flag</mtext><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">true/false</mtext></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">anchor</mtext><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">"keywords..."</mtext></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">args</mtext><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">color</mtext><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">"red"</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">shape</mtext><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">"point"</mtext><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;/tool_call&gt;</mtext></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{aligned} &amp;\texttt{&lt;tool\_call&gt;}\{\\
&amp;\quad\texttt{name}:\texttt{"Visual Prompt Generator"},\\
&amp;\quad\texttt{flag}:\texttt{true/false}\\
&amp;\quad\texttt{anchor}:\texttt{"keywords..."}\\
&amp;\quad\texttt{args}:\{\texttt{color}:\texttt{"red"},\texttt{shape}:\texttt{"point"}\}\\
&amp;\}\texttt{&lt;/tool\_call&gt;}\end{aligned}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</span></div></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="0" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <span id="S3.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">name</span> invokes the visual module, <span id="S3.SS2.p2.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">anchor</span> specifies the textual target derived from reflection for localization, and <span id="S3.SS2.p2.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">args</span> defines the rendering attributes for visual prompts.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Visual Reflection:</span> Upon receiving <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, the generator <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> executes a two-stage pipeline. First, it employs Molmo-7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deitke et al., 2025</a>)</cite> to ground the text <span id="S3.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">anchor</span> into point coordinates. Second, these coordinates are used as prompts for SAM 2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ravi et al., 2024</a>)</cite> to generate precise visual markers (e.g., masks or bounding boxes) overlaid on the original image, and we obtain a new image <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reasoning Refinement:</span> The resulting image <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, now explicitly highlighting the neglected or misinterpreted regions, is fed back into the VLM. This closes the loop, forcing the model to re-attend to the visual evidence (<math id="S3.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>) alongside the query history before generating the next reasoning step.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Training for Reflective Reasoning</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We utilize our constructed visual reflective dataset <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔻</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{D}</annotation></semantics></math> (detailed in Section <a href="#S4" title="4 Visual Reflective Dataset Construction ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) to train the target VLM via Supervised Fine-Tuning. The training objective is designed to optimize the model’s ability to iteratively execute a closed-loop reasoning process.
We formulate the training objective as a multi-turn auto-regressive loss. Formally, for a training sample <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(I_{0},q,\mathcal{Y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(I_{0},q,\mathcal{Y})</annotation></semantics></math>, we maximize the likelihood of the structured sequence over <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> turns:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\min_{\theta}\mathbb{E}_{(I_{0},q,\mathcal{Y})\sim\mathbb{D}}\bigg[-\sum_{k=1}^{K}\log\pi_{\theta}\big(a_{k},r_{k},v_{k}\mid I_{k-1},q,h_{&lt;k}\big)\bigg]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mi>θ</mi></munder><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mi>𝔻</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">[</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mi>log</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min_{\theta}\mathbb{E}_{(I_{0},q,\mathcal{Y})\sim\mathbb{D}}\bigg[-\sum_{k=1}^{K}\log\pi_{\theta}\big(a_{k},r_{k},v_{k}\mid I_{k-1},q,h_{&lt;k}\big)\bigg]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{&lt;k}=\{a_{j},r_{j},v_{j}\}_{j=1}^{k-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{&lt;k}=\{a_{j},r_{j},v_{j}\}_{j=1}^{k-1}</annotation></semantics></math> represents the input history, and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{k-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{k-1}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the visual input processed by the visual prompt generator in the previous turn. This objective ensures that the model learns to jointly optimize its initial answer (<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>), reflective capability (<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>), and tool usage (<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18746v1/dataset.png" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:804/350;" width="804" height="350" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S3.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of the ReflectV dataset construction pipeline. We transform external feedback into self-reflection using Qwen2.5-7B and ensure visual grounding via Molmo-7B and SAM 2.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Visual Reflective Dataset Construction</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To facilitate self-reflection in complex reasoning, we construct a high-quality dataset <span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ReflectV</span> via a multi-agent pipeline, as illustrated in <a href="#S3.F3" title="In 3.3 Training for Reflective Reasoning ‣ 3 Method ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, comprising multi-turn dialogue construction, text processing, and vision processing.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Multi-Turn Dialogue Construction</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To construct a robust foundation for reflective reasoning, we adopt the data curation pipeline proposed in FIRE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024c</a>)</cite>. Instead of relying solely on existing conversational datasets, we transformed multimodal QA pairs into multi-turn dialogues. Specifically, we employ GPT-4V <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2023</a>)</cite> to simulate a “Student-Teacher” interaction based on ground truth annotations where the “Student” generates initial attempts containing potential errors, while the “Teacher” provides a score <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and progressive feedback until the correct answer is reached, effectively converting static QA samples into rich correction histories.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Dialogue Filtering Strategy</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To guarantee the instructional quality of the reflective trajectories, we enforce a rigorous filtering protocol based on the evaluation score <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> assigned to each turn <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. A dialogue trajectory is preserved only if it strictly adheres to the following criteria. Steady improvement: The scores must exhibit a strictly ascending trend (<math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t+1}&gt;s_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t+1}&gt;s_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>), ensuring that the model demonstrates a valid pathway of error correction rather than fluctuating reasoning; Successful convergence: The dialogue must conclude with a perfect score (<math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\text{final}}=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\text{final}}=10</annotation></semantics></math>), indicating that the reflection successfully resolved the initial error; Ground Truth alignment: Beyond the teacher’s score, the final student response must be semantically consistent with the dataset’s ground truth, preventing false positives where the verifier might be misled.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Visual Grounding via Keyword Extraction</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To prevent reflection from degenerating into text-only speculation, we explicitly ground the introspective process with task-adaptive keywords that are later used as tool arguments for visual prompting (<a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Tool-Augmented Visual Prompt Generation ‣ 3 Method ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>). Specifically, for general VQA, we parse entity-centric keywords directly from the reflection. In contrast, for dense perception tasks (e.g., OCR, ChartQ) where reflection lacks spatial specificity, we derive precise keywords from ground truth annotations. To ensure strict alignment between textual thought and visual evidence, we inject visual attribute descriptions (e.g., <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“as indicated by the red point”</span>) back into the reflection text. This visually grounded text is then paired with the marker-overlaid image to constitute a composite input for the subsequent iteration.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Self-Reflective Conversion Mechanism</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To endow our model with self-correction capabilities, we propose a Self-reflective Conversion mechanism. Specifically, we prompt Qwen2.5-7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang and others, 2024</a>)</cite> to rewrite the Teacher’s corrective feedback (e.g., <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“No, your answer is incorrect…”</span>) into a first-person reflective thought process (e.g., <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“Wait, upon closer inspection, I realize my previous answer was incorrect…”</span>). This effectively transforms external criticism into self-reflection, teaching the model <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">how</span> to diagnose its own errors.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Visual Verification and Trajectory Adaptation</h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure precise visual grounding and maintain a balanced training distribution, we implement a dual-stage pipeline after being processed by the visual tool:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Visual Consistency Filtering.</span> We employ a verifier, Qwen2.5-VL-7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> to assess the semantic consistency between the generated visual prompts and texts. This step ensures that the generated marks accurately align with the entities described in the corrective feedback, filtering out instances of ungrounded or ambiguous visualization.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>: </span><span id="S4.T1.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Performance comparison on General Capabilities and OCR &amp; Document Benchmarks. <td id="S4.T2.7.1.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.8.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">7B</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.8.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.8.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">87.95</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.8.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.8.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">68.24</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.8.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.8.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">69.13</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.8.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.8.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">46.01</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.8.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.8.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">76.44</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.8.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.8.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">27.30</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T2.7.1.9" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">
<th id="S4.T2.7.1.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">MIRROR<span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">(ours)</span></span></th>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.9.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">7B</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.9.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">94.42</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.9.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">82.02</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.9.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">72.88</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.9.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">51.49</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.9.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">83.77</span></td>
<td id="S4.T2.7.1.9.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.9pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.7.1.9.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">28.29</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adaptive Trajectory Formatting.</span> Based on verification, we curate a hybrid composition: Reflective chains preserve verified multi-turn trajectories to supervise the closed-loop correction process; Truncated QA collapses failed or redundant sequences into QA pairs (<math id="S4.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{0},q\rightarrow a_{\text{final}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{0},q\rightarrow a_{\text{final}}</annotation></semantics></math>), bypassing the intermediate states. This strategy eliminates noisy signals and mitigates “failure-first” bias, ensuring capabilities for both iterative correction and efficient one-pass inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiment</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To comprehensively assess the performance of our model, we utilize the VLMEvalKit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Duan et al., 2024</a>)</cite> framework, a standardized toolkit for evaluating VLMs. We employ GPT-4o-mini <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hurst et al., 2024</a>)</cite> as the judge to evaluate the correctness of the model’s responses if needed for some specific benchmarks. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation across diverse benchmarks tailored to specific multimodal capabilities. For General Capabilities, we employ MM-Vet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, MMStar <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and SeedBench2-Plus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024b</a>)</cite>. In the domain of OCR &amp; Document Understanding, we utilize TextVQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Singh et al., 2019</a>)</cite>, OCRBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024b</a>)</cite>, and ChartQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Masry et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. To assess Hallucination and robustness, we include POPE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and HallusionBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guan et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Furthermore, we evaluate Fine-grained Perception using HRBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025c</a>)</cite>, MME-RealWorld-Lite <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and VStarBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu and Xie, 2023</a>)</cite>, alongside MathVision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024</a>)</cite> for mathematical reasoning tasks. For further details on the dataset and experimental setup, including discussions on data quality and the effectiveness of trajectory adaptation, please refer to Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Dataset Setting ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendices</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Comparison With Base Models</h3>

<figure id="S5.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18746v1/real_case.png" id="S5.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/272;" width="476" height="272" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F4.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S5.F4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Qualitative examples of iterative visual reflection.<span id="S5.F4.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Compared to the baseline Qwen2.5-VL and the tool-free variant, MIRROR successfully corrects initial perception and reasoning errors.
</span>Top (Spatial Reasoning):<span id="S5.F4.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The model initially misses the “green cylinder” (Round 1). By triggering the visual prompt generator to mark the neglected object with a blue circle, it successfully recounts and corrects the answer in Round 2.
</span>Bottom (Object Identification):<span id="S5.F4.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Addressing the hallucination where the chair is neglected, the model uses the cyan point to actively verify the visual features, confirming the presence of “the chair”.
</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare MIRROR with SOTA MLLMs, including Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, LLaVA-OneVision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, across a comprehensive suite of benchmarks as shown in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.5 Visual Verification and Trajectory Adaptation ‣ 4 Visual Reflective Dataset Construction ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tables</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.5 Visual Verification and Trajectory Adaptation ‣ 4 Visual Reflective Dataset Construction ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. As illustrated, MIRROR consistently outperforms its base model and other strong baselines. The discussions are categorized into three key dimensions:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">General Capabilities and Math Reasoning.</span>
On benchmarks evaluating broad multimodal skills and mathematical reasoning, MIRROR demonstrates significant gains over the base models. As illustrated in the top row of <a href="#S5.F4" title="In 5.1 Comparison With Base Models ‣ 5 Experiment ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, standard models often fail in tasks requiring multi-step logic due to attention drift. In contrast, MIRROR actively identifies and resolves logical discrepancies during complex problem-solving. Notably, despite the absence of mathematical data, MIRROR still achieves notable enhancements in foundational mathematical logic.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OCR &amp; Document Understanding.</span>
On text-intensive tasks classified under OCR and Document Understanding, MIRROR achieves state-of-the-art performance. This suggests that our method effectively directs the model’s attention to neglected visual details, overcoming the limitations inherent in one-pass inference, as shown in <a href="#A4.F23" title="In D.2 Qualitative Analysis. ‣ Appendix D More Efficiency analysis and Visualization ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hallucination Mitigation and Fine-grained Perception.</span>
Crucially, MIRROR excels in reducing hallucinations (e.g., <span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+13.36%</span> on HallusionBench) and enhancing fine-grained perception. By anchoring intermediate reasoning in verifiable visual evidence, our method imposes a strong constraint on the trajectory. This efficacy is exemplified in the bottom row of <a href="#S5.F4" title="In 5.1 Comparison With Base Models ‣ 5 Experiment ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>: while baseline models are prone to hallucinating objects due to ambiguous features, MIRROR actively queries the image with visual markers, ensuring the response is grounded in actual visual pixels.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Comparison with Reasoning Models</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To strictly evaluate the effectiveness of our closed-loop visual reflection mechanism, we also compare MIRROR with two representative reasoning paradigms: <span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Text Reflection</span>, exemplified by VL-Rethinker <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, which employs text-based self-reflection to force rethinking; and <span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Thinking with Images</span>, which equips VLMs with active visual capabilities. The latter includes PixelReasoner <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, DeepEyes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and Adaptive-CoF <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, which utilize operations like zoom-in or selective search. We selected one representative benchmark from each major category to ensure a comprehensive assessment.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T3.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>: </span><span id="S5.T3.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Performance comparison with SOTA reasoning methods, which are all fine-tuned on Qwen2.5-VL-7B. <td id="S5.T3.7.5.5" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.5.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">52.98</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T3.7.6" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T3.7.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.6.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">DeepEyes</span></th>

<td id="S5.T3.7.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.6.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">87.70</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.7.6.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.6.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">49.50</span></td>

<tr id="S5.T3.7.7" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T3.7.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.7.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Adaptive-CoF</span></th>

<td id="S5.T3.7.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.8.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">92.00</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.7.8.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.8.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">94.42</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.7.8.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.8.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">51.49</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.7.8.5" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 0.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.8.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">66.70</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#S5.T3" title="In 5.2 Comparison with Reasoning Models ‣ 5 Experiment ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, MIRROR achieves superior performance by addressing the inherent limitations of both paradigms. First, text-based reflection suffers from hallucination; for instance, VL-Rethinker scores lowest on POPE (84.19), confirming that self-correction without visual grounding is speculative. Second, while “Thinking with Images” models introduce active visual tools, they operate in an open-loop, feed-forward manner, lacking an error-correction mechanism to rectify perceptual failures. In contrast, MIRROR incorporates a closed-loop verification process. MIRROR surpasses the strongest baselines by significant margins—+3.90 on OCRBench and +5.12 on POPE—validating that looking again is only effective when coupled with reflective verification. For more efficiency analysis and visualization, please refer to <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D More Efficiency analysis and Visualization ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Ablation Experiments</h3>

<section id="S5.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.3.1 </span>Training Paradigm &amp; Model Size</h4>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Impact of Reflective Training Paradigm.</span>
To disentangle the benefits of our closed-loop reflective mechanism from the intrinsic quality of the domain-specific knowledge in ReflectV, we compare MIRROR against MIRROR-QA, a variant that is fine-tuned on the same dataset but reformatted into standard single-turn QA pairs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#S5.T4" title="In 5.3.1 Training Paradigm &amp; Model Size ‣ 5.3 Ablation Experiments ‣ 5 Experiment ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, while MIRROR-QA outperforms the Qwen2.5-VL baseline due to domain adaptation, the full MIRROR model achieves higher gains. This empirical evidence confirms that supplementary data alone is insufficient for robust grounding; the explicit process of <span id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">looking again</span>—modeled via reflection and tool usage—is the decisive factor in mitigating hallucinations and correcting errors.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T4.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="S5.T4.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Ablation study on training paradigms and model sizes. The best and second-best results are highlighted in <span id="S5.T4.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">bold</span> and <span id="S5.T4.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">underlined</span>, respectively.</span></figcaption>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Scalability across Model Sizes.</span>
We further investigate the universality of our approach by applying MIRROR to a smaller architecture. As detailed in <a href="#S5.T4" title="In 5.3.1 Training Paradigm &amp; Model Size ‣ 5.3 Ablation Experiments ‣ 5 Experiment ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, the consistent performance improvements across both 3B and 7B scales demonstrate that our framework is model-agnostic. Remarkably, the MIRROR-3B model even surpasses the larger 7B baseline on several benchmarks. This suggests that equipping smaller models with active visual verification capabilities is a parameter-efficient strategy to achieve reasoning performance comparable to larger backbones.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.3.2 </span>Tool Usage</h4>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Quantitative results, as shown in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.5 Visual Verification and Trajectory Adaptation ‣ 4 Visual Reflective Dataset Construction ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and <a href="#S4.T2" title="In 4.5 Visual Verification and Trajectory Adaptation ‣ 4 Visual Reflective Dataset Construction ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, demonstrate that removing the visual prompt generator leads to significant performance drops, particularly on grounding-heavy tasks like MME-RealWorld-Lite (-5.48%) and POPE (-6.47%).
This necessity of active verification is visually evidenced in Fig. <a href="#S5.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 5.1 Comparison With Base Models ‣ 5 Experiment ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. In the object counting case (top row), the tool-free variant correctly MIRROR(w/o tool) suspects an error but, lacking specific visual feedback, fails to locate the hidden “green cylinder” and hallucinates a wrong count.
In contrast, MIRROR explicitly marks the overlooked region, successfully grounding its reflection in pixel-level evidence. Notably, even without tool usage, MIRROR (w/o tool) consistently outperforms the Qwen2.5-VL-7B baseline across most benchmarks, demonstrating the robust intrinsic reasoning capabilities fostered by our reflective training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.3.3 </span>Trajectory Adaptation</h4>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To evaluate the effectiveness of our hybrid trajectory adaptation strategy, we investigate the impact of <math id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>, defined as the ratio of multi-turn reflective chains, as shown in <a href="#S5.T5" title="In 5.3.3 Trajectory Adaptation ‣ 5.3 Ablation Experiments ‣ 5 Experiment ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>. Training exclusively on multi-turn reflective data (<math id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>) leads to a significant performance degradation. This decline is primarily attributed to a <span id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“failure-first”</span> bias, where the model over-fits to error-correction patterns and begins to doubt its own correct reasoning steps even when no errors are present. Conversely, lower ratios (<math id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho\leq 0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho\leq 0.6</annotation></semantics></math>) fail to provide sufficient supervision for complex verification, whereas our balanced strategy with <math id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.75</annotation></semantics></math> achieves the optimal performance across all metrics, effectively harmonizing efficient standard inference with robust reflective refinement.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 5</span>: </span><span id="S5.T5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Ablation study on the multi-turn sample ratio <math id="S5.T5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> for trajectory adaptation conducted on MM-Vet across different capabilities.</span></figcaption>
