</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we have presented <span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR</span>, a framework that enhances multimodal reasoning by transforming reflection from a purely textual revision into an active, closed-loop visual verification process. To facilitate this, we construct <span id="S6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ReflectV</span>, a high-quality dataset designed to teach models to explicitly ground their reasoning in specific image regions. Our experiments demonstrate that MIRROR significantly outperforms strong baselines, validating that equipping VLMs with the agency to “look again” and verify visual evidence is essential for reducing hallucinations and achieving robust reasoning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Despite its effectiveness, our approach currently faces limitations <span id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">in abstract domains</span> and <span id="S6.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">coarse-grained attribute binding</span>, where spatial anchoring is inherently difficult. We provide a detailed analysis of these constraints in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Limitation ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>. Future work will focus on enhancing the granularity of the verification process and exploring mechanisms to anchor symbolic reasoning within visual contexts.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents work aimed at advancing Vision-Language Models by enhancing their reasoning capabilities and mitigating hallucinations. By enabling models to verify their outputs against visual evidence, our framework, MIRROR, contributes to the development of more reliable, grounded, and trustworthy AI systems. While all AI advancements carry potential societal implications, this work primarily focuses on improving technical robustness and correctness, and we do not foresee any specific negative societal consequences that must be highlighted here.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Dataset Setting</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Data Sources</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We construct a high-quality visual reflective instruction-tuning dataset comprising approximately 24k samples. The data sources are curated from diverse public benchmarks, including COCO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2014</a>)</cite>, LLaVA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, GQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hudson and Manning, 2019</a>)</cite>, TextVQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Singh et al., 2019</a>)</cite>, OCRVQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mishra et al., 2019</a>)</cite>, DOCVQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mathew et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, DVQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kafle et al., 2018</a>)</cite> and ChartQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Masry et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. These samples cover a wide range of visual domains and reasoning complexities, serving as the foundation for our fine-tuning process.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure balanced capability acquisition, we categorize these sources into four primary domains: <span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">General QA</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Scene Text (OCR)</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Document Understanding</span>, and <span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Chart Reasoning</span>. As illustrated in <a href="#A1.F5" title="In A.1 Data Sources ‣ Appendix A Dataset Setting ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>(a), this domain-specific distribution is strategically balanced to retain generalizability while boosting fine-grained perception. Furthermore, the statistics regarding the data filtering process and trajectory depth are detailed in <a href="#A1.F5" title="In A.1 Data Sources ‣ Appendix A Dataset Setting ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>(b) and (c), respectively.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18746v1/data_distribution.png" id="A1.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/129;" width="476" height="129" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A1.F5.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="A1.F5.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Statistics and distribution of the ReflectV dataset construction.<span id="A1.F5.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
(a). </span>Domain Distribution:<span id="A1.F5.8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The composition of the raw data spans four distinct capabilities: General QA, Document Understanding (Doc), Scene Text (OCR), and Chart Reasoning.
(b). </span>Filtering Pipeline:<span id="A1.F5.8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The data volume retention across the three construction stages (Original <math id="A1.F5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Response-Filtered <math id="A1.F5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> GT-Filtered), illustrating the rigorous quality control process described in <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Dialogue Filtering Strategy ‣ 4 Visual Reflective Dataset Construction ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.
(c). </span>Trajectory Depth:<span id="A1.F5.8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> We set the default mixing ratio to <math id="A1.F5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.75</annotation></semantics></math> for our training. The distribution of samples based on the number of reflective rounds required for convergence illustrates the varying complexity of error correction.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Data Filtering</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To demonstrate the effectiveness of our filtering strategy and the high quality of our data, we conducted a comparative quality scoring of the filtered, unfiltered, and discarded subsets, and further validated our approach by benchmarking our model against a baseline trained on raw, unfiltered data.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">First</span>, we conducted a blind quality assessment involving both human experts and GPT-4o-mini. We randomly sampled 100 trajectories from three subsets: the discarded noisy data (<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{noise}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{noise}</annotation></semantics></math>), the raw unfiltered data (<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{raw}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{raw}</annotation></semantics></math>), and our final filtered data (<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{clean}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{clean}</annotation></semantics></math>). Each sample was scored on a scale of 1 to 5 based on <span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Logical Coherence</span> and <span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Visual Validity</span>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.T6" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A1.T6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 6</span>: </span><span id="A1.T6.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Comparative quality assessment.<span id="A1.T6.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> We evaluate samples from Discarded (<math id="A1.T6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{noise}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{noise}</annotation></semantics></math>), Unfiltered (<math id="A1.T6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{raw}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{raw}</annotation></semantics></math>), and Filtered (<math id="A1.T6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{clean}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{clean}</annotation></semantics></math>) subsets. The results demonstrate that our pipeline effectively isolates high-quality trajectories.</span></span></figcaption>
<table id="A1.T6.6" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

</table>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As reported in <a href="#A1.T6" title="In A.2 Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Dataset Setting ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{clean}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{clean}</annotation></semantics></math> consistently achieves the highest scores (Avg. <span id="A1.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">4.74</span>), significantly surpassing the raw baseline (<math id="A1.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{raw}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{raw}</annotation></semantics></math>, 3.39). Conversely, the discarded subset (<math id="A1.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{noise}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{noise}</annotation></semantics></math>) exhibits the lowest performance, particularly in visual validity (<span id="A1.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1.42</span>). This distinct stratification confirms that our pipeline effectively identifies and prunes samples with hallucinated or ungrounded visual prompts, ensuring high-quality training data. For more visualization of <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{noise}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{noise}</annotation></semantics></math>, please refer to <a href="#A1.F7" title="In A.2 Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Dataset Setting ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figures</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and <a href="#A1.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ A.2 Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Dataset Setting ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<div id="A1.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Second</span>, we constructed a baseline named <span id="A1.SS2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR-Raw</span>. This variant was fine-tuned on the unrefined dataset (<math id="A1.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>35k samples) obtained before our <span id="A1.SS2.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-turn Dialogue Data Filtering</span> and <span id="A1.SS2.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Visual Verification</span> stage, containing noisy instances where visual reflection was either absent or failed verification.</p>
</div>

<td id="A1.T7.8.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">65.19</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.4.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">56.54</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.4.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">61.47</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.4.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">54.12</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.4.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.4.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">59.04</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.4.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.4.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">58.81</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A1.T7.8.5" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">
<th id="A1.T7.8.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.5.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">MIRROR-0.75</span></th>
<td id="A1.T7.8.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.5.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">69.90</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.5.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">60.77</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.5.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.5.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">70.80</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.5.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.5.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">61.62</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.5.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.5.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">64.40</span></td>
<td id="A1.T7.8.5.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 3.0pt;"><span id="A1.T7.8.5.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#ECECEC;">66.70</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">As presented in Table <a href="#A1.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ A.2 Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Dataset Setting ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, we assess the efficacy of our visual verification filter by comparing the unrefined baseline, <span id="A1.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR-Raw</span>, against <span id="A1.SS2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MIRROR-1.0</span> (<math id="A1.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>). It is crucial to note that both variants share an identical structural composition—consisting exclusively of multi-turn reflective trajectories (<math id="A1.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>)—which isolates <span id="A1.SS2.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">data quality</span> as the sole variable.
Despite MIRROR-Raw utilizing a significantly larger corpus (<math id="A1.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>35k samples), it underperforms the filtered MIRROR-1.0 (<math id="A1.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>24k samples) across all metrics.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Specifically, MIRROR-Raw lags behind the structure-aligned MIRROR-1.0 (55.87 vs. 58.81) and exhibits a substantial deficit compared to our optimal hybrid model, MIRROR-0.75 (55.87 vs. 66.70). This massive performance gap confirms that data purity is paramount; retaining <math id="A1.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>11k noisy samples—where visual grounding is hallucinated or absent—introduces conflicting signals that severely hamper the model’s potential. In contrast, removing this noise enables the precise optimization seen in MIRROR-0.75.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Implementation Details</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Training Details.</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We utilize LLaMA-Factory <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2024</a>)</cite> to perform Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on the Qwen2.5-VL-7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. The training is conducted on 2 <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> NVIDIA H100 GPUs for 3.0 epochs. To ensure training efficiency and memory optimization, we utilize the DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 optimization and employ Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> for parameter-efficient fine-tuning. The LoRA rank is set to <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=32</annotation></semantics></math> with the scaling factor <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=128</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Inference Details.</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We perform all evaluations using the SFT-adapted MIRROR model. And we use the same hardware settings in all experiments. To ensure high-quality visual grounding, the visual prompt generator is powered by Molmo-7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deitke et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, which predicts precise point coordinates based on the model’s textual reflection. For mask generation, we employ the SAM 2.1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ravi et al., 2024</a>)</cite> model, specifically loading the large-scale checkpoint <span id="A2.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">sam2.1_hiera_l.pt</span> to ensure robust segmentation performance even in complex visual scenes.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F10" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18746v1/inference_rounds.svg" id="A2.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:286/198;" width="286" height="198"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="A2.F10.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Distribution of inference trajectory lengths across representative benchmarks.<span id="A2.F10.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The stacked bars illustrate the percentage of samples resolved within 1, 2, or 3+ rounds.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Trajectory Length Analysis.</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To understand the model’s dynamic behavior, we conducted a statistical analysis of the inference trajectories across evaluated benchmarks, as illustrated in <a href="#A2.F10" title="In B.2 Inference Details. ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.
We observe that the model adaptively adjusts its reasoning depth based on the inherent difficulty of the task:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Efficiency in Information Extraction:</span> For straightforward queries where visual evidence is explicit, the model tends to converge efficiently. For instance, on ChartQA, which primarily involves direct value extraction, 98.7% of samples are resolved within a single round, minimizing unnecessary computational overhead.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rigor in Complex Perception:</span> In contrast, for tasks requiring fine-grained verification or hallucination mitigation, the trajectory extends significantly. On MME-RealWorld and HallusionBench, the model engages in a second round of visual reflection for 58.6% and 57.0% of cases, respectively. Notably, MathVision exhibits the highest proportion of trajectories exceeding three rounds (2.5%), reflecting the need for iterative correction in multi-step logical derivation.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Overall, with <span id="A2.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">80.2%</span> of total samples resolved in the first turn, this distribution confirms that MIRROR effectively balances efficiency and rigor, engaging in deep visual reflection only when the complexity of the query demands it.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Prompt</h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Prompt for Dataset Construction</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To construct the training data for the ReflectV dataset, we employ a multi-stage prompting strategy to transform raw annotations into grounded, first-person reflective trajectories.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">First, we generate task-specific visual cues. For data-intensive tasks like Charts, OCR, and Doc, we utilize a specific prompt to extract key subjects and entities as shown in <a href="#A3.F11" title="In C.1 Prompt for Dataset Construction ‣ Appendix C Prompt ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>. For general QA tasks, we employ a two-step process: in <a href="#A3.F12" title="In C.1 Prompt for Dataset Construction ‣ Appendix C Prompt ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>, first identifying key physical objects mentioned in the feedback, and subsequently merging them into a concise caption. Next, we use a caption insertion prompt, as shown in <a href="#A3.F13" title="In C.1 Prompt for Dataset Construction ‣ Appendix C Prompt ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, to seamlessly blend these visual cues (e.g., specific marks or coordinates) into the corrective feedback, ensuring the text is visually grounded. Finally, in <a href="#A3.F14" title="In C.1 Prompt for Dataset Construction ‣ Appendix C Prompt ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>, to simulate an internal self-correction process, we apply a role conversion prompt that transforms the content from a “teacher’s evaluation” perspective into a “student’s first-person reflection” (e.g., changing ”Your response is wrong” to “I think my response is wrong”).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F11" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18746v1/chart_caption.svg" id="A3.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/466;" width="476" height="466"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F11.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="A3.F11.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Subject Extraction Prompt: Extracts core subjects and key modifiers from questions to form concise visual descriptions for Chart, OCR, and Doc understanding tasks.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A3.F12" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18746v1/qa_caption.svg" id="A3.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/433;" width="476" height="433"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F12.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 12</span>: </span><span id="A3.F12.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Visual Caption Generation Prompt: A two-step pipeline that first identifies key physical objects from feedback and then synthesizes them into short descriptive captions for QA tasks.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A3.F13" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18746v1/insert_caption.svg" id="A3.F13.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/341;" width="476" height="341"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F13.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 13</span>: </span><span id="A3.F13.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Caption Insertion Prompt: Seamlessly integrates generated visual captions and spatial marks (e.g., points) into textual feedback to ensure visual grounding.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A3.F14" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18746v1/self_reflective_conversion.svg" id="A3.F14.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/402;" width="476" height="402"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F14.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 14</span>: </span><span id="A3.F14.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Self-Reflective Conversion Prompt: Rewrites teacher-side evaluations into first-person student self-reflections (e.g., changing ”Your response is wrong” to ”I think my response is wrong”).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Prompt for Iterative Reasoning</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To enable the model with self-reflection and visual verification capabilities, we design a structured system prompt and user prompt that enforces a rigorous output protocol, as shown in <a href="#A3.F16" title="In C.2 Prompt for Iterative Reasoning ‣ Appendix C Prompt ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> and <a href="#A3.F17" title="In C.2 Prompt for Iterative Reasoning ‣ Appendix C Prompt ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F15.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18746v1/system_prompt_1.svg" id="A3.F15.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="width:47.415em; height:48.081em;aspect-ratio:630/639;" width="630" height="639"></object>

</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A3.F16" class="ltx_figure">
<figure id="A3.F16.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18746v1/system_prompt_2.svg" id="A3.F16.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="width:47.312em; height:57.759em;aspect-ratio:628/767;" width="628" height="767"></object>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>More Efficiency analysis and Visualization</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Efficiency Analysis.</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To evaluate the real-world practicality of MIRROR, we conduct a comparative analysis of inference efficiency on the MM-Vet dataset, employing average inference time per sample and average token consumption as metrics. As detailed in Table 8, we benchmark our method against representative baselines from two paradigms: Text Reflection (VL-Rethinker) and Thinking with Images (PixelReasoner, DeepEyes, Adaptive-CoF).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 8: </span>Efficiency comparison on the MM-Vet dataset. We report the average time cost (seconds) and token consumption per sample. The best results are highlighted in <span id="A4.T8.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">bold</span>. The results demonstrate that MIRROR achieves state-of-the-art efficiency.</figcaption>
<table id="A4.T8.8" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A4.T8.8.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A4.T8.8.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="A4.T8.8.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Method</span></th>

<td id="A4.T8.8.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A4.T8.8.6.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">5.06</span></td>
<td id="A4.T8.8.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A4.T8.8.6.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">197.51</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A4.T8.8.7" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A4.T8.8.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row"><span id="A4.T8.8.7.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Adaptive-CoF</span></th>
<td id="A4.T8.8.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A4.T8.8.7.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">4.02</span></td>
<td id="A4.T8.8.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A4.T8.8.7.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">143.51</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A4.T8.8.8" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A4.T8.8.8.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A4.T8.8.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">MIRROR (Ours)</span></th>
<td id="A4.T8.8.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A4.T8.8.8.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">3.73</span></td>
<td id="A4.T8.8.8.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A4.T8.8.8.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">112.58</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Compared to the Text Reflection model: Our method reduces inference time by 32.9% (3.73 s vs. 5.56 s) and token consumption by 50.9% (112.58 vs. 229.33) compared to VL-Rethinker. This significant reduction suggests that our targeted visual verification mechanism effectively circumvents the verbose and redundant self-correction chains often required by purely text-based reflection.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Compared to Thinking with Images models: MIRROR significantly outperforms PixelReasoner (64.12 s) and DeepEyes (5.06 s) in terms of latency. Even compared to the highly efficient Adaptive-CoF, MIRROR maintains a distinct advantage, further reducing time cost by 7.2% and token usage by 21.5%. These findings confirm that MIRROR not only enhances reasoning accuracy but also ensures an efficient inference process, making it highly suitable for practical deployment.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Qualitative Analysis.</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond quantitative metrics, we provide comprehensive qualitative comparisons across diverse complex reasoning scenarios.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with Base Model.</span> <a href="#A4.F19" title="In D.2 Qualitative Analysis. ‣ Appendix D More Efficiency analysis and Visualization ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figures</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> and <a href="#A4.F20" title="Figure 20 ‣ D.2 Qualitative Analysis. ‣ Appendix D More Efficiency analysis and Visualization ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> illustrate the reasoning trajectories of our model versus the base model Qwen2.5-VL-7B, highlighting our model’s ability to self-correct.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with Competitive Baselines.</span> We further compare MIRROR with two representative reasoning paradigms: (i) the ”Thinking with Images” approach (PixelReasoner, DeepEyes, Adaptive-CoF), and (ii) the textual self-reflection approach (VL-Rethinker). As illustrated in <a href="#A4.F23" title="In D.2 Qualitative Analysis. ‣ Appendix D More Efficiency analysis and Visualization ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figures</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>, <a href="#A4.F26" title="Figure 26 ‣ D.2 Qualitative Analysis. ‣ Appendix D More Efficiency analysis and Visualization ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">26</span></a>, <a href="#A4.F29" title="Figure 29 ‣ D.2 Qualitative Analysis. ‣ Appendix D More Efficiency analysis and Visualization ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">29</span></a> and <a href="#A4.F31" title="Figure 31 ‣ D.2 Qualitative Analysis. ‣ Appendix D More Efficiency analysis and Visualization ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">31</span></a>, MIRROR demonstrates superior grounding and error correction capabilities.</p>
</div>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Limitation</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To provide a comprehensive understanding of MIRROR’s boundaries, we present qualitative examples of failure cases in the figures below. These cases correspond to the two primary limitations discussed in the main paper: the difficulty in grounding abstract concepts and the lack of granularity in complex attribute binding.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1. Limited Applicability in Abstract Domains.</span>
Despite these improvements, MIRROR still faces challenges in symbolic derivation involving complex spatial mapping. <a href="#A5.F33" title="In Appendix E Limitation ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">33</span></a> illustrates a geometry problem requiring the calculation of a circle’s radius using the Pythagorean theorem. While the model correctly performs the symbolic derivation in the text, its attempt to invoke the visual prompt generator is ineffective. The model tries to ground the concept of “diameter calculation and radius division” into visual points. However, mathematical operations and logical variables are abstract concepts that lack a direct spatial mapping in the 2D image plane. Consequently, the generated visual cues (red points) provide no informative feedback for verifying the correctness of the arithmetic steps.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2. Coarse-grained Attribute Binding.</span>
Furthermore, MIRROR encounters difficulties in fine-grained attribute binding under compositional constraints. As shown in <a href="#A5.F34" title="In Appendix E Limitation ‣ MIRROR: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning via Reflection On Visual Regions" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">34</span></a>, the user queries for a specific flower defined by a compositional constraint: <span id="A5.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“five petals and three leaves.”</span> Although the underlying LLM correctly identifies the target option (E) via textual reasoning, the visual tool fails to strictly enforce these count-based attributes. Instead of isolating the specific target, the tool generates coarse visual markers (green points) on <span id="A5.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">all</span> flower instances in the image. This indicates that the visual prompt generator struggles to distinguish complex attribute combinations, defaulting to a generic object detection behavior (detecting ”flowers”) rather than precise constraint verification.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F32.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18746v1/failure_case1_1.png" id="A5.F32.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="width:47.375em; height:55.206em;aspect-ratio:787/917;" width="787" height="917" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F32.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="A5.F32.sf1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Part 1 of Qualitative failure case 1.<span id="A5.F32.sf1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F33" class="ltx_figure">
<figure id="A5.F33.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.18746v1/failure_case1_2.png" id="A5.F33.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="width:47.181em; height:43.663em;aspect-ratio:784/725;" width="784" height="725" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F33.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="A5.F33.sf1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Part 2 of Qualitative failure case 1.<span id="A5.F33.sf1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> </span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F33.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 33</span>: </span><span id="A5.F33.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Limited Applicability in Abstract Domains:<span id="A5.F33.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> When addressing mathematical problems, the model attempts to verify symbolic logic (e.g., radius calculation) visually. However, since abstract derivations cannot be spatially grounded, the resulting visual prompts (red points) are uninformative and do not aid in verifying the calculation.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F34" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18746v1/failure_case2.png" id="A5.F34.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:476/632;" width="476" height="632" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F34.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 34</span>: </span><span id="A5.F34.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Coarse-grained Attribute Binding: <span id="A5.F34.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">This case demonstrates the limitations of the current visual verification mechanism.
</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
